item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 29 July 2026
item.description:
Brennan argues today’s games industry is too expensive, unfinished, and exploitative, making the backlog you already own look smarter by the day.

CrazyKinux digs into EVE Online’s bedrock rules—equal consequences, spaceships first, and nowhere truly safe—as the sandbox’s load-bearing philosophy.

Bhagpuss breaks down Neverness To Everness’s cat-run scratchcard event, where cheap tickets feel predictable and the 50k cards bring the real gamble.

Shintar finally maxed every primary Midnight profession to 100, mostly in-house with alts, spreadsheets, purple tools, and a lot of Abundance runs.

Scopique likes Tempus Gameit as an easier way to auto-track playtime across Steam, GOG, Epic, Battle.net, Heroic, and screenshots too.

Wilhelm says REPO shines as chaotic co-op slapstick, where fumbling gravity-gun loot runs and hilariously broken valuables matter more than actually succeeding.

Andrew Plotkin rounds up Mysterium side news: the Myst documentary inches along, fan Age Jalargura is out, and Myst Online’s Descent keeps evolving.

UltrViolet shares stable PET scan news, worries over a worsening right-hand issue, Blaugust prep, and a small helping of Final Fantasy XIV.

Tim Bray makes a warm pitch for amateur music camp: lots of live unamplified playing, older attendees, and real brain-health benefits.

Mike turns a weirdly pricey 1985 BBC Bridge Companion into Bridgetris, a delightfully nerdy Z80-and-VRAM hardware hacking project.

Dave Winer sees a new WordPress-to-RSS.chat bridge as a big open-web moment, with RSS acting more like a social web protocol again.

Jeromai uses a GPT-4o prompt as a springboard into blogging motives, process, and what even counts as a post heading into Blaugust.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 28 July 2026
item.description:
Stargrace cleared over a million in WoW despite spotty auction posting, then cut back from 20 servers to 10 to rebuild consistency.

Shintar hopped into SWTOR master mode flashpoint pugs for fun, from a smooth Esseles run to a late-night Shrine of Silence marathon.

Luna enjoyed Fortune Fragments’ mix of visual novel vibes and hex-tile rune puzzling, with each reading adding fresh twists to the foreteller routine.

Oya says Arranger’s clever row-and-column puzzle mechanics and sincere story made it the perfect low-stress palate cleanser during a gaming slump.

Marc uses Elevator Action Returns to show just how dramatically arcade design evolved between 1983 and 1994, without losing the original’s punch.

Ellie tackles Castlevania: Rondo of Blood via Dracula X Chronicles, digging into version choices and Richter Belmont’s place in the series.

Wilhelm maps out the long Pokemon Go grind to 50 platinum medals, weighing Pokedex gaps, catch goals, and what Niantic still hasn’t released.

Anarchae spins off a standalone links post, touching on DRM-free ebooks, Ursula K. Le Guin’s house, a new Ottawa fantasy bookstore, and more.

Tipa wrestles with AI’s convenience versus its climate, labor, and coding fallout, especially when work all but forces LLMs into the loop.

Cliffski explains why he’d rather juggle investments than people, and says LLMs have been surprisingly useful for financial research.

Bruce Schneier flags Cognyte’s FalcoNet van as yet another Stingray-style cell-site simulator letting cops sweep up nearby phones en masse.

Magi argues Blaugust should spotlight human, imperfect, personal creation, while pushing back on harassment around this year’s AI policy.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 27 July 2026
item.description:
Kimimi finds Get Bass 2 trades the original’s arcade sparkle for slower, fussier fishing sim vibes that demand patience and exploration.

Wilhelm tracks another tight Fantasy Critic week, with Splatoon Raiders scoring up and Avatar Legends arriving as a big question mark.

The Chronicler runs three Ramla battles in Commands & Colors Medieval, turning one crossroads into a neat little Crusades mini-campaign.

Tobold finds Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous’ Through the Ashes refreshingly low-level but punishing, fiddly, and worth lowering the difficulty for.

Michael rounds up Myst news from Mysterium, including the painful reveal of canceled prototype Project Anglerfish and word of more universe plans.

Jamie Zawinski drops a one-line TV gag wondering which bottle-blonde dirtbag is Igor the Carpathian.

Warner puts Sunday Morning Reading on hiatus for a travel weekend and points desperate readers toward the archives instead.

Juhis argues open source and small software projects don’t need endless growth, and that building for a specific audience is perfectly valid.

Dave Winer posts RSS.chat API docs, a WordPress connector, and a very Dave case for open feeds over centralized subscription silos.

Roger pieces together Tolkien’s account of Sauron’s fall, arguing Gil-galad and Elendil overthrow him before Isildur delivers the final blow.

Patrick shares a gloriously weird Veins of the Earth monster roster and digs into encounter tables built for usability, tone, and DIY worldbuilding.

WCRobinson maps out a modest Blaugust return, honoring Belghast while aiming for weekly posts and shorter, sharper game reviews.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 26 July 2026
item.description:
Shintar mourns World of Warcraft’s short-lived Decor Duels and uses the shutdown to gripe about Blizzard calling content evergreen while PvP queues languish.

Wilhelm and his daughter push Stardew Valley through winter, unlocking the quarry and mine carts, hitting mine level 120, and suffering through all that fishing.

Michael celebrates Llamasoft’s Moose Life as a trippy, ceiling-flipping arcade shooter that feels uniquely its own, even among Jeff Minter’s usual riffs.

Roger says Cold Storage looks like disposable sci-fi horror, but David Koepp’s fungus outbreak thriller turns out to be a modestly fun evening watch.

Bhagpuss rounds up a music-heavy week, arguing Charli xcx’s B-sides like “If You Take Away The Music” and “Playboy Bunny” outshine the singles.

Ramen Junkie’s week mixes confusing World Cup stoppage time, a pricey tire blowout, and small retail wins like vinyl hunting and passing on Leader Laser Prime.

Tipa turns mountain-spotting into a geography puzzle, climbing Heublein Tower to figure out which Connecticut peaks are actually visible from her desk.

Brennan argues the IndieWeb needs real Quebec French terminology, not just borrowed English, to lower barriers and make the scene feel less anglophone by default.

Jamie Zawinski blasts the dependence on Instagram and X after Meta briefly suspended The Stud’s account, warning against outsourcing critical communications to hostile platforms.

Dave Winer pitches the web’s open ethos, notes RSS.chat now has a REST API, and shares code, docs, and an example blog-builder app.

UltrViolet checks in on chemo side effects, dunks on Dungeon Crawler Carl’s non-ending and audiobook voice, and wrestles with AI-image tensions around Blaugust.

Ghastly gives a friendly Blaugust 2026 primer, pitching August blogging, community participation, and the event’s role in honoring Belghast’s legacy.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 25 July 2026
item.description:
Tipa compares her dense, bustling Pokopia island with her daughter’s serene utopia, musing on how our game worlds reflect who we are.

Shintar loved SWTOR’s Legacy Reborn update, praising its character moments, big Star Wars feels, and the lack of KOTOR-style cutscenes.

Owls is rolling into EverQuest Legends on Freeport with a shadow knight/necromancer/shaman, sold on multiclassing and a more solo-friendly Norrath.

Scopique walks through his Star Citizen fleet, from mining rigs and cargo tools to homestead defense and a couple of niche combat ships.

David’s Gunderholfen session sends rival guilds chasing the Ravens through sabotaged dungeon paths before a swamp basilisk crashes the party.

Wilhelm rounds up EverQuest news, from EverQuest Legends launching July 28 to the Lethar TLP server starting with The Serpent’s Spine.

The Chronicler spotlights Baltic Empires, a GMT strategic wargame where asymmetric powers vie for Baltic dominance through war, trade, and state-building.

Andrew Plotkin shares Witness feelie scans and a fun correction: the matchbook’s “long life” symbol turned out to be real Chinese, not a fake gag.

Anarchae checks in on work, budgets, Blaugust plans, Zelda, TV, and anthology reading while bracing for the resume-and-cover-letter grind.

Jimmy points readers to a new Analog Antiquarian piece on Richard III, a quick cross-link for the history-minded.

JJM argues his stalled gamedev projects happen when he chases cool engine code instead of building an actual game first.

Jeromai pivots from a GPT-4o letter about society to Blaugust, blogging, and “claudefishing” as a murky Claude-adjacent Substack trend.
